_comment: Tier-2 Layer-C: skfem linear_elasticity numerical-correctness gate. Cross-backend mirror of fenics elasticity_mms_convergence — same manufactured u = (sin(πx)·sin(πy), sin(2πx)·sin(2πy)), same plane-strain E=1.0/ν=0.3, but DIFFERENT catalog API: MeshTri.refined + ElementVector(ElementTriP1()) + BilinearForm with sym_grad + trace + ddot + LinearForm with f = -μ·Δu - (λ+μ)·grad(div(u)) computed analytically (vs UFL-symbolic auto-derive in fenics). Asserts P1 h=1/32 L2 error <= 1.3e-2 and P1 EOC h=1/16 → h=1/32 in [1.7, 2.3]. CROSS-BACKEND NUMERICAL AGREEMENT with fenics: skfem P1=8.96e-3 vs fenics P1=8.99e-3 (0.3% diff); skfem EOC=1.924 vs fenics EOC=1.925 (identical to 3 sig figs). Verified against skfem 12.0.1 on 2026-06-01. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable, INVERTED direction -- this is a Layer-C correctness gate that executes no pathology, so the control ACTIVATES the documented constitutive mistake instead of removing one): T2_MUTATE=1 makes the strain measure eps() inside the stiffness BilinearForm the full grad() instead of sym_grad(), so the assembled operator is no longer the Navier operator whose -div(sigma) the analytic LinearForm implements. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1 / NGSolve 6.2.2604: the unmutated run matches all 5 expect_in_output strings; those five are bare key prefixes and survive by construction, but T2_MUTATE=1 drives P1_h32_l2err from 8.957911e-03 to 2.346078e-01 and the EOC from 1.924 to 0.054, tripping both bars so the FORBIDDEN string 'FAIL:' appears and the fixture goes red. FINDING established while building this control: the manufactured u vanishes identically on the whole boundary of the unit square, so the ElementVector interleaved-dof Dirichlet block is numerically inert -- replacing it with plain zeros reproduces every printed number bit-for-bit. It is neither a usable mutation site nor evidence that the interleaving convention is exercised. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
